ashok: FYI saw 3 OOMs on gpt3-small-prod last night around 09:12 UTC. All on nodes with high prefix/cache pressure after the kernel switch.
kai: ugh. which kernel change? the matmul tiling tweak? :thinking_face:
ashok: yeah, the new int8 tiling landed in #PR-492. perf-bot flagged a regression earlier: p99 up ~6% on a subset. logs attached below.
perf-bot: regression detected: p99 latency +6.1% (window 02:00-06:00 UTC), error rate stable.
mike: can you paste the OOM trace? interested if it was workspace alloc failing vs fragmentation.
ashok: here's the relevant allocator trace (trimmed):
```
2026-11-09T09:12:11Z [allocator] alloc_workspace(size=72, model=gpt3-small) -> tried_pool=true
2026-11-09T09:12:11Z [kv-cache] shard=13 evict_candidate_count=0 used=1.9GiB/2.0GiB
2026-11-09T09:12:11Z [cuda] cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
2026-11-09T09:12:11Z [runtime] fallback -> attempt spill-to-host=true
```
kai: looks like a workspace request bumped into near-full shard memory. Two directions: shrink workspace prealloc or reduce per-shard max memory.
emily: we have three levers here that interact: workspace sizing, allocator pool growth policy, and prefix-cache shard sizing/TTL.
jordan: my quick sim yesterday showed that increasing shard count from 16->32 reduces per-shard footprint but increases metadata and sweep overhead; hit-rate slightly improved for small-ish prompts (<512 tokens) because collisions drop.
mike: proposal A: keep kernel change, but cap workspace prealloc to 64MB for gpt3-small and enable buffer reuse across generation steps. That reduces temporary high-water by ~120MB per request in my bench.
ashok: proposal B: aggressive shard eviction: reduce per-shard soft_limit to 1.5GiB and lower TTL to 45m (from 2h) for low-traffic customers. That would free memory but might drop hit-rate.
kai: can we do a middle ground: dynamic shard sizing based on observed hit-rate and a background sampler? e.g., if hit-rate < 15% lower shard size, else keep.
emily: dynamic looks attractive but adds complexity. We could start with safety-first mitigations: 1) cap workspace for affected models 2) enable slab reuse (tl;dr allocator patch) 3) add a short-term sweep for shards with zero accesses in last 10m.
perf-bot: note: enabling slab reuse in v0.34 reduced median allocation latency by 8% in staging.
mike: i ran a quick micro-bench: buffer reuse + 64MB workspace cap -> no OOMs under 10k concurrent requests synthetic with current cache pressure; p99 still +2% vs previous kernel but within SLA.
ashok: next steps: kai to revert tiling (hotfix) or add a compatibility flag? mike to prepare allocator patch for slab reuse + pool cap. emily to draft TTL/shard policy change and run simulation vs workload trace.
kai: I'll gate the kernel behind a runtime flag for rollout and short-circuit to old matmul for affected SKUs.
emily: I'll run shard-sizing sweep sim today and share hit-rate vs memory curves. if we can get a plan by EOD we can avoid customer impact.
ashok: thanks. also, add nvtx markers to workspace allocs so we can correlate kernel hotpaths with allocations next time. small change but will help root cause.
mike: added to my todo. will send short PR with test + benchmark.
ashok: ok closing here for now — will follow up with sim results and PRs. :thumbsup:
